name.en: Fake bank call in Maltese: “let’s cancel the transaction”

how.mt: Tirċievi SMS b’link, imbagħad telefonata minn numru li jidher Malti. Mara li titkellem Malti tajjeb (xi drabi vuċi magħmula bl-intelliġenza artifiċjali) tgħid li hi mid-dipartiment tal-frodi tal-bank, issejħilek b’ismek u tistaqsik jekk għamiltx xiri b’iPhone f’xi raħal. Meta tgħid le, tibagħtlek link biex “tikkanċella” t-tranżazzjoni, iżda l-link iwassal għal paġna falza li tixbah lil tal-bank. Malli tispiċċa t-telefonata, il-flus jinħarġu mill-kont lejn kontijiet barra minn Malta.
how.en: You get a text with a link, then a call from what looks like a Maltese number. A woman speaking fluent Maltese (sometimes an AI-generated voice) says she is from the bank’s fraud department, calls you by your name and asks whether you made a purchase with an iPhone in some town. When you say no, she sends a link to “cancel” the transaction, but it opens a fake page that looks like your bank. As soon as the call ends, money leaves your account for accounts outside Malta.

text.mt: Tasal SMS b’link li tidher qisha mill-bank.
text.en: A text with a link arrives that looks like it is from your bank.

text.mt: Iċemplulek minn numru Malti. Mara titkellem bil-Malti, tgħid li hi mill-frodi tal-bank u ssejħilek b’ismek.
text.en: A Maltese number calls. A woman speaking Maltese says she is from the bank’s fraud team and uses your name.

text.mt: Tistaqsik dwar xiri b’iPhone jew pagament ta’ ċertu ammont li ma tagħrafx.
text.en: She asks about an iPhone purchase or a payment of a certain amount that you don’t recognise.

text.mt: Tibagħtlek link biex “twaqqaf” il-pagament. Il-paġna tixbah lil tal-bank u titolbok tidħol fil-kont.
text.en: She sends a link to “stop” the payment. The page looks like your bank and asks you to log in.

text.mt: Wara t-telefonata, il-flus jinħarġu lejn kontijiet barra minn Malta.
text.en: After the call, money is sent out to accounts abroad.

text.mt: Bonġu Josephine, jien Claire mill-uffiċċju tas-sigurtà tal-bank. Qed inċempillek għax dalgħodu deher xiri ta’ €689 b’iPhone f’Ħaż-Żabbar. Int għamiltu? Le? Allura issa nibagħtlek messaġġ fuq il-mowbajl, agħfas fuqu u nwaqqfuh flimkien qabel ma jgħaddi.
text.en: Good morning Josephine, I’m Claire from the bank’s security office. I’m calling because a €689 purchase on an iPhone in Żabbar showed up this morning. Did you make it? No? Then I’ll send you a message on your mobile now, tap on it and we’ll stop it together before it goes through.

mt: mara qaltli li hi mill-frodi tal-bank
numru Malti qal li hu l-bank
en: woman said she was from bank fraud
sent me a link to cancel the transaction
Maltese number said it was my bank

mt: Il-bank ma jibgħatlekx link biex tikkanċella tranżazzjoni.
Telefonata mhux mistennija dwar xiri li ma għamiltx, segwita minn link.
Numru Malti jew isem il-bank fuq l-iskrin ma jfissirx li hu l-bank: in-numri jistgħu jiġu ffalsifikati.
en: Banks don’t send a link to cancel a transaction.
An unexpected call about a purchase you didn’t make, followed by a link.
A Maltese number or the bank’s name on screen doesn’t prove it is your bank: numbers can be faked.

mt: Aqta’ t-telefonata u ċempel lill-bank fuq in-numru fuq wara tal-kard jew fl-app.
Tagħfasx links li jaslu b’SMS jew waqt telefonata.
Jekk dħalt fil-link jew ħarġu l-flus, ċempel lill-bank minnufih u rrapporta lill-Pulizija. Żomm screenshots u n-numru li ċemplek.
en: Hang up and call your bank on the number on the back of your card or in its app.
Don’t tap links sent by text or during a call.
If you opened the link or money left your account, call your bank at once and report it to the Police. Keep screenshots and the number that called.
